title: Duties
description: Recurring tasks services must or should have done – an access review every quarter, a restore test every month. Each period is judged by the real runs of the duty's process.
panelHint: Periods follow the server's time zone ({{tz}}). Only real runs of the process count – never dry runs.
emptyApplication: No duty of a service is about this application.
emptyListHint: Duties are defined on the page of a service.
archiveConfirm: Archive the duty “{{name}}”? Its stored periods stay; no new periods are judged.
scheduleDryRun: dry runs – they do not count
graceDaysHint: Days into the next period a run may still end (and a late run start).
remindDaysHint: 0: no reminder. The owners get it once per period while the duty is not done.
ownersHint: user:<name> or team:<name>. Without owners, the service owners are responsible.
name: Name
pendingSkips_one: {{count}} exception waits for a second person
pendingSkips_other: {{count}} exceptions wait for a second person
historyHint: Closed periods are stored for good: later changes of the duty or the process do not change them.

skips.title: Exceptions
skips.reasonHint: Why the duty is skipped for this period. A second person approves it.
skips.asked: Exception asked for – a second person decides
skips.fourEyes: Four-eyes principle: someone else decides the exception you asked for.

closedEarly.archived: closed early: the duty was archived
closedEarly.endedArchived: Ended without a run – duty archived
closedEarly.endedChanged: Ended without a run – duty changed

endsCurrentArchive: The current period {{period}} has no run that counts yet. Archiving records it as “ended without a run”, and it counts as not met.
endsCurrentChange: You change how the duty is judged. The current period {{period}} has no run that counts yet: it is recorded as “ended without a run” and counts as not met. The new rules start now.
